ap_statistics-m01.set_intro: A manager records the number of hours that each of ten employees trained and the number of errors that each made in a week. The scatterplot shown displays the data, with the least-squares line $\hat{y} = 15.97 - 0.97x$ for all $10$ observations and $r = -0.84$. One employee is highlighted: its training time is $8$ hours and its number of errors is $14.6$ errors.

stimulus.description: Scatterplot of number of errors versus training time

data.title: Number of errors versus training time

items.stem: What is the residual of the highlighted observation? (Use the given line and round to two decimal places.)

options.text: $6.39$ errors
options.why: The residual is the actual value minus the predicted value: $14.6 - (8.21) = 6.39$.

options.text: $-6.39$ errors
options.why: Subtracts in the wrong order; the residual is the actual value minus the predicted value.

options.text: $22.36$ errors
options.why: Leaves the intercept out of the predicted value before subtracting.

options.text: $8.21$ errors
options.why: Reports the predicted value instead of the residual.

items.stem: The highlighted observation is removed, and the least-squares line and the correlation are recalculated from the other observations. Which of the following describes the change?

options.text: The correlation would decrease in strength and the slope would change very little.
options.why: Does not match the recalculated values: the strength of the correlation goes from $|r| = 0.84$ to $0.98$, which is an increase, not a decrease.

options.text: The correlation would increase in strength and the slope would change very little.
options.why: Without the highlighted point $|r|$ changes from $0.84$ to $0.98$, while the slope changes from $-0.97$ to $-0.99$, a change of only about $2\%$.
